explanation: A man from the hill country of Ephraim, also known as Mika, who is the main character in chapter 17 of the book of Judges.
Objects or images that represent deities and are worshiped instead of the true God.
A metallic element often associated with wealth and value. Micah used silver coins to make an idol and other religious objects.
Micah's mother, who blesses him and encourages him to make religious objects from the silver he returned to her.
A person from the tribe of Levi, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Levites had special religious roles and duties, including service in the temple.
A religious leader who performs ceremonies and sacrifices on behalf of the people. In Judges 17, a young Levite becomes priest for Micah and his family.
The act of honoring and showing reverence to a deity, usually through prayer, song, and rituals.
